newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia gets good news on economy.
newsitem.headline: Australia gets good news on economy.

text.p: Australia received some positive economic news on Wednesday when an international ratings agency boosted the country's credit outlook and the statistics bureau announced an improvement in retail sales.

Moody's Investors Service said from New York that the outlook for Australian's sovereign debt rating, downgraded from the perfect AAA to Aa2 in the 1980s, was improving because of steady fiscal policies and a prudent interest rate strategy.
The agency, which wields considerable power in international bond markets, said economic growth and fiscal tightening in recent years had cut the underlying budget deficit in recent years.
That cut had allowed Australia to reduce its reliance on foreign debt. Moody's said a ratings upgrade would depend on Australia further reducing its reliance on offshore funding.

Shortly afterwards, the official Bureau of Statistics announced that retail sales had risen by 2.9 percent in May against the previous month to reach a seasonally-adjusted value of A$10.59 billion (US$7.94 billion).
Market forecasts had centred around a 2.0 percent rise and the data saw the Australian dollar and bonds firm slightly.
But economists cautioned that the figure was always volatile and not much should be read into it.
"Unfortunately, I don't think it really gives us the definitive answer we have been looking for," said Michael Blythe, senior economist at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Australian financial markets have been waiting for the Reserve Bank of Australia to announce what would be a fifth rate cut in the past year after holding its monthly board meeting on Tuesday.
Any signs of an economic pick-up -- coupled with the possibility of increased U.S. rates -- could persuade the RBA to hold off on further easing.
Citibank Australia chief economist Stephen Koukoulas said the retail sales were a bit stronger than they had forecast but noted that it followed two monthly falls.
"I wouldn't say the retail sector is booming yet, it is encouraging to see a bit of growth coming through but I think the best you could say is the worst is behind us," he said.
